text: {"distance_m": 2.3, "reasoning_short": "This is a rough estimate, not a measured value. A 15% contrast spot is well below the 100% contrast that 20/20 acuity (1 arcmin) assumes. So I used contrast-detection limits instead. For small targets, Ricco's law says the threshold scales roughly with contrast × area, i.e. C·α² ≈ constant. Blackwell-type indoor data give about 100% contrast needed at ~1 arcmin, so 15% contrast needs α ≈ 1/√0.15 ≈ 2.6 arcmin. Allowing for indoor rather than bright lighting, I took ≈3 arcmin (≈8.7×10⁻⁴ rad). Distance ≈ 2 mm / 8.7×10⁻⁴ rad ≈ 2.3 m."}
